discover.lexicon.cert.ce-kennzeichnung.w: A declaration by the manufacturer that the product meets every EU directive applying to it. Not a quality seal and not issued by anyone: you affix it yourself and you carry the liability.
discover.lexicon.cert.rohs-konformität.w: Limits ten hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment, among them lead, mercury, cadmium and four phthalates. Evidenced by supplier declarations and, where in doubt, by testing.
Obliges you to know the substances in the product, to pass on any Substance of Very High Concern above 0.1 percent by weight down the chain, and to notify SCIP.
discover.lexicon.cert.eu-ecolabel.name: EU Ecolabel
discover.lexicon.cert.eu-ecolabel.what: The voluntary EU environmental label. Criteria are set per product group and cover the whole life cycle; it is awarded by a national competent body after assessment.
discover.lexicon.cert.eu-energy-label.wh: The A to G efficiency scale, mandatory for many appliance categories. The product must also be registered in EPREL before it may be placed on the market.
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-9001.name: ISO 9001
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-9001.what: Quality management system standard. It certifies how the organisation works, not what the product is, and customers and tenders often require it regardless.
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-14001.name: ISO 14001
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-14001.what: Environmental management system standard: how the organisation identifies, controls and improves its environmental impact.
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-45001.name: ISO 45001
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-45001.what: Occupational health and safety management. Increasingly requested in supplier audits alongside ISO 9001 and ISO 14001.
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-50001.name: ISO 50001
discover.lexicon.cert.iso-50001.what: Energy management system standard. In several member states it unlocks energy tax relief, which is often the real reason companies pursue it.
discover.lexicon.cert.oeko-tex-standard-: Tests textiles for harmful substances at every stage, from yarn to finished garment. Limits are stricter than the law requires, and stricter again for baby articles.
discover.lexicon.cert.gots-global-organi: Organic textiles: at least 70 percent certified organic fibres, plus social and environmental criteria across the whole processing chain.
discover.lexicon.cert.fair-trade.name: Fair Trade
discover.lexicon.cert.fair-trade.what: Guarantees a minimum price and a premium to producers, mostly for agricultural raw materials such as cotton, cocoa and coffee.
discover.lexicon.cert.bsci.name: amfori BSCI
discover.lexicon.cert.bsci.what: A social audit programme for the supply chain. It produces an audit report, not a certificate — a distinction that matters when a customer asks for proof.
discover.lexicon.cert.sa8000.name: SA8000
discover.lexicon.cert.sa8000.what: Certifiable social accountability standard covering child labour, forced labour, working hours, pay and freedom of association.
discover.lexicon.cert.grs-global-recycle: Verifies recycled content and tracks it through the chain of custody, together with social and environmental requirements at each processing step.
discover.lexicon.cert.fsc.name: FSC
discover.lexicon.cert.fsc.what: Responsible forestry for wood, paper and cardboard. Watch the label variants: 100 percent, Mix and Recycled are not interchangeable claims.
discover.lexicon.cert.blauer-engel.name: Blue Angel
discover.lexicon.cert.blauer-engel.what: The German state environmental label, in place since 1978. Criteria are set per product group and are tightened periodically, so an award is time-limited.
discover.lexicon.cert.cradle-to-cradle.w: Assesses material health, circularity, renewable energy, water stewardship and social fairness, and awards a level from Bronze to Platinum.
discover.lexicon.cert.nordic-swan.name: Nordic Swan Ecolabel
discover.lexicon.cert.nordic-swan.what: The official environmental label of the Nordic countries. Frequently demanded in Scandinavian public tenders, which is where it earns its keep.
discover.lexicon.cert.epd-environmental-: A verified, standardised life-cycle report. It declares environmental impact rather than certifying that the impact is good, which is a common misreading.
discover.lexicon.cert.energy-star.name: ENERGY STAR
discover.lexicon.cert.energy-star.what: An energy efficiency programme originating in the US. Within the EU it applies mainly to office equipment and is largely superseded by the EU energy label.
discover.lexicon.cert.ul-listed.name: UL Listed
discover.lexicon.cert.ul-listed.what: Safety testing by Underwriters Laboratories, effectively expected for the North American market. It is not a substitute for CE marking in the EU.
discover.lexicon.cert.tüv.name: TÜV mark
discover.lexicon.cert.tüv.what: A test mark from a technical inspection body. Always check which mark and which scope: the name alone says nothing about what was actually tested.
discover.lexicon.cert.gs-zeichen.name: GS mark (tested safety)
discover.lexicon.cert.gs-zeichen.what: The German voluntary mark for tested safety, awarded by an approved body. Voluntary in law, but treated as a de facto requirement by much of German retail.
